name: Skyveil Reach
description: A high-altitude mountain zone above the Bone Wastes. Windswept peaks, crumbling warden ruins, and thin air. The last Warden fortress -- Stormcrown Keep -- looms at the highest point. Ancient warden magic has kept this place preserved but corrupted since the Seal Wars.

rooms.name: Mountain Pass
rooms.description: The bone-strewn wastes fall away behind you as the terrain rises sharply into dark stone foothills. A narrow pass cuts between two sheer cliff faces, the rock scarred with ancient tool marks where the Wardens once widened this road. Wind funnels through the gap with enough force to stagger you, carrying the smell of wet stone and ozone. The switchback trail above is barely visible through curtains of low cloud.

interactables.description: A section of the trail is covered in loose, unstable gravel that could give way at any moment.

actionData.noticeMessage: The gravel ahead looks loose and unstable -- testing your footing before committing would be wise.
actionData.triggerMessage: The scree gives way beneath you! You slide downward on a cascade of loose stone!
actionData.saveMessage: You catch a solid outcrop as the gravel slides past, pulling yourself back to stable ground.
actionData.failMessage: Sharp rocks tear at your legs as you tumble down the scree slope, slamming against a boulder.

rooms.name: Highland Trail
rooms.description: An exposed ridge trail climbs steeply along the mountain's shoulder, offering dizzying views of the Bone Wastes far below. The path is barely wide enough for two abreast, its edges crumbling into empty air. Warden waymarkers line the route -- carved stones with the sealed-eye symbol, most weathered to illegibility. To the east, a ruined structure clings to a rocky spur. The wind howls through gaps in the stone with a voice that sounds almost human.

rooms.name: Crumbling Watchtower
rooms.description: The remains of a Warden watchtower perch on a rocky spur, three of its four walls collapsed into rubble. The surviving wall still bears carved reliefs depicting armored figures standing vigil over the mountain passes. A cracked observation slit looks out over the Bone Wastes, and rusted iron brackets suggest signal fires were once lit here. The floor is treacherous -- loose flagstones over a drop that goes down farther than the eye can follow.

rooms.name: Windswept Crossing
rooms.description: Four paths converge at a broad shelf of bare stone, scoured clean by the relentless mountain wind. A massive Warden waystone stands at the center -- a pillar of dark granite twice the height of a man, its sealed-eye symbol still faintly luminous despite centuries of erosion. The wind changes direction unpredictably here, creating swirling vortices of grit and snow that sting exposed skin. To the west, rows of pale shapes are visible through the haze. To the east, a ridge crackles with distant lightning.

rooms.name: Warden Graveyard
rooms.description: Rows of weathered tombstones march across a sheltered depression in the mountainside, each carved with the sealed-eye symbol and a name in the old Warden script. The dead were interred standing, in the Warden tradition, their graves marked by upright stone slabs that lean at angles after centuries of frost heave. Some graves have been disturbed -- the earth sunken or pushed outward from below, as if the occupants tried to claw their way free. A cold, greenish light seeps from the deepest cracks.

interactables.label: Grave Eruption
interactables.description: The earth around one grave is bulging upward, hairline cracks radiating outward. Something beneath is building pressure.

actionData.noticeMessage: That grave is bulging outward -- the earth around it could erupt at any moment.
actionData.triggerMessage: The grave erupts! Shards of stone and bone explode outward in a violent burst!
actionData.saveMessage: You throw yourself behind a tombstone as debris whistles past, peppering the stone at your back.

rooms.name: Wind-Carved Cave
rooms.description: A natural cave hollowed from the mountainside by centuries of wind erosion, its entrance a smooth oval worn into the rock face. The interior is surprisingly deep, the walls sculpted into flowing organic shapes by the tireless work of grit-laden air. The wind moans through the cave in a low, continuous drone that sets the teeth on edge. Old Warden supply caches -- rotted crates and corroded metal containers -- line the back wall, long since looted of anything useful.

rooms.name: Forgotten Shrine
rooms.description: A small stone shrine nestled in a sheltered nook of the mountainside, its entrance framed by two carved pillars depicting Wardens in ceremonial armor. The shrine's interior is surprisingly well-preserved -- the sealed-eye symbol on the back wall still glows with a faint golden warmth, and offerings have been left on the altar: mountain flowers that have not wilted despite the cold, a cup of water that has not frozen. Someone tends this place still, in secret.

effects.message: The shrine's ancient wards hold firm against the corruption above.

rooms.name: Storm Ridge
rooms.description: A jagged ridge of dark stone juts eastward from the crossing, its surface blackened and fused where lightning has struck again and again over the centuries. The air here is thick with ozone and crackles with static -- metal objects hum and spark, and the hair on your arms stands straight. Deep score marks in the rock trace the paths of old lightning channels, branching like river deltas frozen in stone. The ridge offers no shelter from the storm above.

interactables.label: Lightning Strike Zone
interactables.description: The ridge here is directly beneath a gap in the clouds. Lightning channels converge on this point -- the rock is still warm from the last strike.

actionData.noticeMessage: The rock here is warm and the air is thick with ozone -- another strike is imminent.
actionData.triggerMessage: Lightning hammers down from the thunderhead! A bolt of raw electricity strikes the ridge where you stand!

actionData.failMessage: The lightning catches you mid-stride, every muscle seizing as current tears through your body.

rooms.name: Precipice Lookout
rooms.description: The ridge terminates in a sheer drop, a promontory of blackened stone jutting out over a cloud-filled void. The view is staggering -- through gaps in the storm, the entire eastern face of the mountain range is visible, peak after peak marching to the horizon in shades of grey and white. A Warden signal platform stands at the promontory's tip, its fire channels cold and filled with rainwater. The wind is savage here, coming in gusts strong enough to push you toward the edge.

rooms.name: Sky Bridge
rooms.description: A massive stone bridge spans the chasm between two peaks, built by the Wardens to connect the lower approaches to the upper mountain. The bridge is a single unsupported arch of fitted stone blocks, each carved with interlocking Warden seals that once held the structure together through magic as much as masonry. The seals are failing now, cracks webbing through the keystone, and the wind threatens to tear you from the span with every gust. The chasm below is bottomless cloud. Crossing feels like walking on nothing.

interactables.description: The keystone of the bridge is webbed with deep cracks. Fragments of carved stone shift underfoot with each step.

actionData.noticeMessage: The stones ahead are shifting -- the bridge is weakest at the keystone. Tread carefully.

actionData.failMessage: You plunge through the gap and barely catch a protruding stone, the impact slamming the breath from your lungs.

rooms.name: Eagle Aerie
rooms.description: A high nesting ground crowns the peak beyond the sky bridge, its rocky surface littered with enormous nests woven from branches, bone, and strips of old Warden banners. Feathers as long as your forearm drift on the wind. The nests are large enough to sleep in, built by whatever massive raptors have claimed this height as their domain. The view from the aerie is commanding -- the entire mountain range spreads below, and the dark bulk of Stormcrown Keep is visible above to the northwest, wreathed in perpetual lightning.

rooms.name: Skyveil Plateau
rooms.description: Above the crossing, the mountain opens into a broad plateau that gives the zone its name -- a shelf of stone perpetually veiled by low-hanging storm clouds that obscure the peaks above. The plateau was once a Warden staging ground, and the foundations of barracks, storehouses, and a command post are still visible as raised stone platforms with mounting holes for palisade walls. The sealed-eye symbol is carved into the central platform, large enough to be seen from the air. Paths lead in every direction from this central hub.

rooms.name: Ruined Barracks
rooms.description: The collapsed remains of a Warden barracks sprawl across a shelf of rock west of the plateau. Three of the four walls have fallen inward, burying whatever was inside under tons of fitted stone. The fourth wall still stands, its arrow slits staring blindly at the mountain. Inside the rubble, fragments of daily life are visible -- a corroded cook-pot, the remains of a bunk frame, a sealed-eye pennant so faded it is barely recognizable. Something has been digging through the debris recently, leaving fresh claw marks on the stone.

actionData.noticeMessage: That lintel above is barely supported -- one wrong vibration could bring it crashing down.

rooms.name: Armory Ruins
rooms.description: The old Warden armory is in better shape than the barracks -- its reinforced walls were built to withstand siege, and while the roof has caved in, the walls themselves still stand. Empty weapon racks line the interior, their contents long since looted or corroded to uselessness. A few iron brackets still hold the rusted ghosts of halberds. The forge at the back of the room is cold and cracked, its bellows rotted away, but the anvil remains -- dark iron, unmarked by time, still ringing faintly when the wind catches it just right.

rooms.name: Cliffside Path
rooms.description: A narrow path hugs the eastern cliff face, barely wide enough for single file. Iron pitons hammered into the rock by Warden engineers provide precarious hand-holds, most rusted but still anchored. The drop to the right is absolute -- hundreds of feet of empty air before the clouds close in. Frozen spray from an unseen waterfall coats the stones in a treacherous glaze of ice, and the path glistens in the storm light. Every step requires concentration.

rooms.name: Frozen Falls
rooms.description: A waterfall cascading down the cliff face has frozen solid, transforming into a wall of blue-white ice that towers overhead. The ice is ancient and compressed, translucent enough to see dark shapes trapped within -- rocks, branches, and what might be the silhouette of an armored figure, perfectly preserved. Meltwater seeps from the base of the falls, feeding a shallow pool that has frozen into a mirror-smooth sheet. The air here is bitterly cold, and the silence after the constant wind is startling.

rooms.name: Archon's Camp
rooms.description: A deep natural alcove in the mountainside has been expanded by careful stonework into a defensible camp. Fresh Warden symbols are carved into the walls -- not ancient and faded like the ones below, but maintained by a living hand. A small forge-fire burns in a stone hearth, its smoke drawn out through a natural chimney. Weapon racks, armor stands, and shelves of scrolls line the walls. The camp has the feel of a place where someone has chosen to stand watch alone for a very long time, maintaining discipline against the encroaching corruption.

rooms.name: Warden Memorial
rooms.description: A large stone memorial stands on an exposed shelf east of the camp, carved from a single block of dark granite the size of a small house. The names of fallen Wardens are inscribed across every surface in precise script, hundreds of them, each accompanied by the sealed-eye symbol and a date. The most recent names are carved deeper, with more care -- these were not ancient history to whoever wrote them, but people remembered and mourned. A ring of smaller standing stones surrounds the memorial, their surfaces inscribed with protective wards that still faintly glow.

rooms.name: Summit Approach
rooms.description: The final stretch of mountain before Stormcrown Keep. The path narrows to a wide Warden-built road, its flagstones cracked but still serviceable, climbing the last hundred yards toward the massive gatehouse visible through the storm above. The corruption from the Keep is visible now -- dark veins of energy run through the rock itself, pulsing like a heartbeat. The air tastes of copper and ozone, and the storm is at its worst here, with lightning striking the road every few seconds.

rooms.name: Stormcrown Gates
rooms.description: The gates of Stormcrown Keep loom before you -- massive doors of dark iron set into a gatehouse of fitted stone that merges seamlessly with the mountain peak itself. The doors stand partially open, warped by the corruption that pulses through the structure like a disease. Beyond them, a passage leads into the Keep's interior, lit by the sickly green glow of inverted Warden seals. The storm is at its most intense here, lightning striking the gatehouse towers in a continuous barrage that the corrupted structure drinks in hungrily.

It hunts with terrifying speed, folding its wings and diving from the clouds in near-silence before striking with bone-breaking force. Its eyes glow with a pale electric blue that suggests the storm's corruption has seeped into its blood.

npcs.description: A battle-scarred elder in battered Warden plate, her white hair cropped close to the skull and a long scar running from her left temple to her jaw. She is the last of the Archons -- the Warden field commanders who led the defense of the Seals. She has held this position alone for years, training anyone with the strength to reach her and the courage to face what waits in the Keep above.

He was the Keep's lorekeeper before Stormcrown fell, and he is the only living person who has been inside the Keep and returned.

The key to reaching him lies with his second-in-command, Warden-Commander Theron, who guards the inner sanctum.
